v1.0.0 — SNR wavelets and Fresnel zones in Rust
First stable release. geoveil-mp now covers the whole advanced multipath pipeline that runs on the [GeoVeil batch platform](https://batch.geoveil-rinex.eu): code multipath and cycle slips per signal, plus SNR wavelet analysis and first Fresnel zone mapping, all in Rust and called from Python. Everything from 0.2 works as before.

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miluta7/geoveil-mp/main/docs/img/fresnel_map.webp" width="420" alt="First Fresnel zone footprints"> <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miluta7/geoveil-mp/main/docs/img/scalogram.webp" width="440" alt="Morlet wavelet scalogram">

## Highlights

- **SNR wavelets per satellite.** SNR is converted to linear amplitude, detrended arc by arc, and passed through a Morlet transform. You get band power in period bands matched to the sampling interval and a 95 % red-noise significance level.
- **First Fresnel zones.** Zone semi-axes and specular-point distance for every 10° × 10° track cell, for any antenna height and carrier (Hunegnaw & Teferle, *Sensors* 2022, eq. 6).
- **About 20× faster, same numbers.** Checked against the numpy reference used on the platform: wavelet power agrees to 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁵. A 1 Hz hour with 51 satellites takes 0.35 s instead of 7.05 s. Satellites run in parallel and the GIL is released.
- **10 new Python functions:** `analyze_snr_wavelets`, `scalogram`, `morlet_cwt`, `band_power`, `red_noise_significance`, `period_bands`, `detrend_arc`, `split_arcs`, `fresnel_zone`, `fresnel_map`.

## Install

```bash
pip install -U geoveil-mp
```

Wheels for Linux, Windows and macOS on Python 3.9 to 3.12.

```python
import geoveil_mp as gm

obs = gm.read_rinex_obs("station.rnx")
w = gm.analyze_snr_wavelets(obs)          # every satellite, in parallel
a, b, dist = gm.fresnel_zone(15.0, 2.0)   # 2 m antenna, 15° elevation -> (4.896, 1.267, 7.464) m
```
